  "methodology_note": "The supplied RANKING WEIGHTS rubric (enamel quality, lid fit, handle construction, etc.) is written for cookware, not a consumable liquid product, so criteria were reinterpreted in olive-oil terms (packaging/oxidation resistance in place of 'durability,' pour-spout/labeling in place of 'ease of use,' etc.) while preserving the stated weights. Olive oil as a class genuinely could be split into meaningful sub-groups — everyday supermarket EVOO versus ultra-premium/boutique finishing oil versus bulk bag-in-box cooking oil — since price per ounce and use-case differ enormously (roughly $0.35–$3.00+ per ounce across the sources reviewed). Per instructions, no such categories were invented; the three picks above represent the best all-purpose, widely-purchasable extra-virgin olive oils across the entire class based on convergence of independent blind tastings (ATK, Wirecutter, Consumer Reports, Serious Eats), with the ATK-supplied source given priority for the #1 slot per sourcing rules. A curator may want to ask for 'everyday' vs. 'premium/finishing' oil categories given how differently priced and used these two segments are."
